newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - April 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - April 17.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Thursday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:
* Tobacco companies have offered to disclose research they conducted into smoking and health to settle disputes.
* Ford's quarterly profit more than doubled to $1.47 billion, beating analysts' expectations.
* Apple Computer reported a quarterly loss which was slightly worse than expectations.
* March industrial production rose 0.9 percent and housing starts fell 6.4 percent in the month.
* The Dow Jones Industrials rose 92.71 to 6,679.87, extending a rally.
* Harcourt General made a $740 million offer to buy National Education, topping a friendly bid by Sylvan Learning.
* An NASD panel ordered four former Stratton Oakmont officers to pay $10 million in punative damages to a California doctor.
* An effort by Chrysler to get rid of some parts-making jobs is the focus of a United Auto Workers strike at some company plants.
* In 1996, General Motors's chairman received a three percent rise in salary and bonus.
* The Supreme Court heard arguments about whether insider trading laws could be applied to people who technically were not insiders.
* Bell Atlantic and NYNEX are preparing for the possibility that the Justice Department might not give the green light to their $23 billion merger.
* Time Warner's posted a modest profit in the first quarter due to a recovery in its cable systems.
* Amgen filed a patent suit against biotechnology firm Transkaryotic that is trying to sell less expensive versions of successful drugs.
* Grain and livestock futures fell on concerns a 62-year-old Indiana man's death might be linked to "mad cow" disease.

* Heard on the Street: A $300 billion pricetag for the tobacco industry to settle its liability for smoking-related damages might seem impossibly expensive, even if stretched out over 25 years. Yet tobacco stocks shot up yesterday.
* Credit markets: Bond prices were little-changed yesterday, after a sharp morning sell-off inspired bargain hunting by investors during the afternoon's trading.
